2-001.note: Removed 'no single external feature is found in every mammal'. Notes now say every mammal has hair or fur at some stage; the whale has sparse hair; limbs and habitat vary.

2-002.note: Mammal notes list the visible external features hair or fur, external ears (pinnae) and whiskers, and say milk and live birth are not visible external features. Item 015 also credits external ears.

2-003.note: Lion hierarchy now ends 'species Panthera leo'.

2-004.note: Worked key step 2 is now 'body divided into ring-like segments' against 'body not divided into segments'.

2-005.note: Item 020 prompt is now 'List two visible external features of a bird.' The bat clause is gone; the second mark is for wings or a beak.

2-006.note: P02(e) answer and guidance now say leg and antenna counts fall in a set range for each group and differ between groups. The 2.1 notes no longer say the leg count is 'fixed'.

2-007.note: Drawing notes now cover labelling adaptive features with their use (waxy cuticle of a desert plant, a beetle's hard wing cases).

2-008.note: Item 019 now credits clawed toes as an alternative second feature.

2-009.note: Fish notes add the gill cover (operculum) and the lateral line. Item 011 credits both (gills or operculum count as one point).

2-010.note: Item 023 stem rewritten: the learner calls a 5-leg-pair, 2-antenna-pair animal an arachnid 'because it has more legs than an insect'. Marks are for naming the error (arachnids have four leg pairs and no antennae) and for the correct group, crustacean, with its features.

2-011.note: Partly fixed: the 2.2 connections now point to 1.2 for fair sampling, variables and means. Re-mapping P03's objective_ids is a work-order change, so it was left as a label question.

2-012.note: Item 022 guidance now asks for proportions that match this specimen as observed, e.g. an ant's abdomen compared with its thorax.
